In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
keratins are expressed in the same pattern in the hamster pouch carcinogenesis model as in the human epidermal carcinogenesis model, with some minor differences.
K13 expression is maintained throughout the carcinogenesis process, whereas K1 expression is lost in the more advanced stages of carcinogenesis.
keratin expression is altered during hamster cheek pouch squamous cell carcinoma development, with a loss of K14 and K1 and preservation of K13.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the keratins 1 and 14 are expressed in the normal hamster cheek epithelium, and their expression is altered during the early stages of 7, 12-dimethyl-benz[a]anthracine-induced carcinogenesis.
the K1 keratins are induced in the hyperplastic epithelia and are expressed in foci of cells that are positive for gamma-glutamly transpeptididase.
the expression of K1 keratin was induced during the early stages of 7, 12-dimethyl benzanthracene-induced carcinogenesis, but was almost absent in later stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the keratin pattern is altered early during carcinogenesis and that the K1 keratins may be good markers for early lesions.
the hamster cheek-pouch model is a good model for studying carcinogenesis and chemically induced alterations in keratin expression.
keratins are good markers of the carcinogenic process and could be used as a tool to monitor the effect of chemopreventive agents.
